Define K=A I. The proof obtains I(G u)=u and G(I u)=u from the two inverse laws,
then K(G u)=A u and G(K u)=A u. AI=IA gives K(A u)=A(K u). Consequently,
  A K A u + G A u = K A^2 u + K G^2 u = K u.
The first equality uses KA=AK and GA=AG=KG^2. The second uses linearity of K
and A^2+G^2=identity. These identities are proved locally, not hypotheses.
The inherited positivity of G supplies its selfadjointness. Symmetry of A,G
therefore transports the last vector equality to the exact mixed inner identity
  <K A u,A v> + <A u,G v> = <K u,v>.
This is the hKMixedVector/hMixed mechanism at lines366-382. It does not require

AG=GA and the two symmetries yield

Moreover G K=A and symmetry give

The mixed/diagonal identities give

Subtracting this expression from the preceding norm expression cancels exactly
